notes.text: Portion: Arithmetic; Concept: Even & Odd Numbers; Formula / Explanation: Even: divisible by 2, Odd: not divisible by 2; Example (if applicable): Even: 2, 4, 6; Odd: 1, 3, 5
Concept: Integers; Formula / Explanation: All positive & negative whole numbers including 0; Example (if applicable): ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3...
Concept: Rational Numbers; Formula / Explanation: Can be expressed as ⁄ (b ≠ 0); Example (if applicable): ½, ¾, -⁵⁄₈
Concept: Irrational Numbers; Formula / Explanation: Cannot be written as𝑎 𝑏 ⁄; Example (if applicable): √2, π, e
Portion: Rounding; Concept: To nearest 10; Formula / Explanation: Look at units digit; Example (if applicable): 87 → 90
Concept: To nearest 100; Formula / Explanation: 𝑎𝑏 Look at tens digit; Example (if applicable): 374 → 400
Concept: To nearest 1000; Formula / Explanation: Look at hundreds digit; Example (if applicable): 3487 → 3000
Portion: Fractions; Concept: Comparing; Formula / Explanation: Cross Multiply: ᵃ⁄ᵇ vs ᶜ⁄ᵈ → a×d vs b×c; Example (if applicable): ²⁄₃ vs ³⁄₅ → 2×5 = 10, 3×3 = 9 → 2⁄3 > 3⁄5
Portion: Percentage; Concept: % to Decimal; Formula / Explanation: x% = x⁄100; Example (if applicable): 25% = 25⁄100 = 0.25
Concept: Value to %; Formula / Explanation: (Part ⁄ Whole) × 100; Example (if applicable): (25⁄200) × 100 = 12.5%
Concept: Increase by x%; Formula / Explanation: Final = Original × (1 + x⁄100); Example (if applicable): 100 increased by 20% = 100 × ¹²⁰⁄₁₀₀ = 120
Concept: Decrease by x%; Formula / Explanation: Final = Original × (1 - x⁄100); Example (if applicable): 100 decreased by 20% = 100 × ⁸⁰⁄₁₀₀ = 80
Portion: Unity Method; Concept: Unit Value; Formula / Explanation: Total Value ⁄ Quantity; Example (if applicable): 5 pens = Rs. 100 → 1 pen = ¹⁰⁰⁄₅ = Rs. 20
Portion: Discount & Sale; Concept: Discount; Formula / Explanation: Discount = List Price × Discount Rate; Example (if applicable): Rs. 500 × ¹⁰⁄₁₀₀ = Rs. 50
Concept: Sale Price; Formula / Explanation: Sale Price = List Price - Discount; Example (if applicable): Rs. 500 - 50 = Rs. 450
Portion: Income Comparison; Concept: A has x% more than B; Formula / Explanation: B = A × ¹⁰⁰⁄(100 + x); Example (if applicable): A = 120, x = 20 → B = 120 × ¹⁰⁰⁄₁₂₀ = 100
Concept: A has x% less than B; Formula / Explanation: B = A × ¹⁰⁰⁄(100 - x); Example (if applicable): A = 80, x = 20 → B = 80 × ¹⁰⁰⁄₈₀ = 100
Portion: Relative % Change; Concept: 2 values x% & y% more than 3rd; Formula / Explanation: Net = x + y + (x × y)⁄100; Example (if applicable): x = 20%, y = 30% → 20 + 30 + 600⁄100 = 56%
Portion: Net % Change; Concept: General Formula; Formula / Explanation: Net = x + y + (x × y)⁄100
Portion: Compound Decrease; Concept: Final Value; Formula / Explanation: Final = Original × (1 - r⁄100)ⁿ; Example (if applicable): 1000 × (⁹⁰⁄₁₀₀)² = 1000 × 0.81 = 810

Concept: Simple Interest (SI); Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ⁄ 100; Explanation / Example: P = Principal (initial amount) - R = Rate of interest per year (%) - T = Time (in years) Example: If P = 1000, R = 10%, T = 2 yrs → 🔹 SI = (1000×10×2)/100 = 200
Concept: Total Amount (A); Formula: A = P + SI; Explanation / Example: Total money after interest period Example: A = 1000 + 200 = 🔹 1200

Concept: Compound Interest (CI); Formula: A = P(1 + R ⁄ 100)ᵗ CI = A − P; Explanation / Example: Compounded annually - CI = Compound Interest Example: P = 🔹 1000, R = 10%, T = 2 yrs A = 1000(1 + 10/100)² = 1000(1.1)² = 1210 → CI = 210
Portion: Ratio; Concept: Basic Form; Formula / Explanation: a : b = ᵃ⁄ᵇ; Example (if applicable): 4:5 = ⁴⁄₅

Concept: Divide Quantity in Ratio; Formula / Explanation: Total = sum of ratios Portion = Total × (individual⁄total ratio); Example (if applicable): Rs. 900 in 2:1 → Total = 3 parts → 2 parts = 600, 1 part = 300
Concept: Proportion Rule; Formula / Explanation: ᵃ⁄ᵇ = ᶜ⁄ᵈ → a×d = b×c; Example (if applicable): Cross multiplication
Concept: Theorem of Alternative Proportion; Formula / Explanation: If ᵃ⁄ᵇ = ᶜ⁄ᵈ, then: (a + c)⁄(b + d) = a⁄b = c⁄d; Example (if applicable): If 2⁄3 = 4⁄6, then (2 + 4)⁄(3 + 6) = 6⁄9 = 2⁄3
Concept: Exponents; Rule / Formula: a⁰ = 1; Explanation / Example: Any non-zero number raised to power 0 is 1. Example: 5⁰ = 1
a¹ = a - Any number raised to power 1 remains same. Example: 7¹ = 7
aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ - Multiply powers with same base. 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷
aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ - Divide powers with same base. 5⁶ ÷ 5² = 5⁴
(aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ - Power of a power = multiply powers. (3²)³ = 3⁶; Rule / Formula: (a × b)ⁿ = aⁿ × bⁿ; Explanation / Example: Distribute power over multiplication. (2 × 5)³ = 2³ × 5³ = 1000
(a ⁄ b)ⁿ = aⁿ ⁄ bⁿ - Distribute power over division. (⁴⁄₅)² = 4² ⁄ 5² = ¹⁶⁄₂₅
a⁻ⁿ = 1 ⁄ aⁿ - Negative exponent means reciprocal. 2⁻³ = 1 ⁄ 2³ = ¹⁄₈
a¹⁄ⁿ = ⁿ√a - Fractional exponent = root. 8¹⁄³ = 8 = 2
aᵐ⁄ⁿ = ⁿ√(aᵐ) - Exponent form to root. 27²⁄³ = (2∛7²) = 729 = 9
Concept: Square Roots; Rule / Formula: √(a × b) = √a × √b; Explanation / Example: ∛ ∛ Multiply square roots. √(4×9) = √4 × √9 = 2×3 = 6
√(a ⁄ b) = √a ⁄ √b - Divide square roots. √(25⁄4) = √25 ⁄ √4 = 5⁄2
√a² = a (if a ≥ 0) - Square root of square is absolute value. √36 = 6
(√a)² = a - Square cancels root. (√7)² = 7
Type: 1. Arithmetic Series; Explanation: Numbers increase or decrease by a fixed value (common difference).; Example: 2, 5, 8, 11, ? → +3 → Ans: 14
Type: 2. Geometric Series; Explanation: Numbers multiply/divide by a fixed ratio.; Example: 3, 6, 12, 24, ? → ×2 → Ans: 48
Type: 3. Square/Cube Series; Explanation: Numbers are perfect squares or cubes (or based on them).; Example: 1, 4, 9, 16, ? → squares → Ans: 25
Type: 4. Alternating Series; Explanation: Pattern changes every second or third term.; Example: 2, 4, 6, 3, 5, 7, ? → Two alternating series: (+2), (+2), ... and (+1), (+1), ...
Type: 5. Prime Number Series; Explanation: Series formed by prime numbers.; Example: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ? → next prime → Ans: 13
Type: 6. Fibonacci Series; Explanation: Each number is sum of previous two.; Example: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ? → Ans: 13
Type: 7. Difference of Differences; Explanation: Second-level difference is constant.; Example: 2, 4, 8, 14, 22, ? → First diff: +2, +4, +6, +8 → Ans: 32
Type: 8. Multiplication + Addition; Explanation: A combo of multiply & add pattern.; Example: 2, 5, 11, 23, ? → ×2 +1, ×2 +1,... → Ans: 47
Type: 9. Half or Double Series; Explanation: Numbers are halved or doubled.; Example: 128, 64, 32, ? → ÷2 → Ans: 16
Type: 10. Mixed Operations; Explanation: Different operations in one series.; Example: 1, 4, 10, 22, ? → ×2 +2, ×2 +2,... → Ans: 46
Type: 11. Decimal/Fraction Series; Explanation: Series involving fractions or decimals.; Example: 1, 1.5, 2.25, 3.375, ? → ×1.5 each step → Ans: 5.0625
Type: 12. Pattern Repetition; Explanation: Repeating fixed pattern or set of numbers.; Example: 1, 3, 5, 1, 3, 5, ? → Repeats every 3 terms → Ans: 1
Type: 13. Series with Squares/Cubes in Between; Explanation: Numbers hidden between squares/cubes.; Example: 3, 9, 27, 81, ? → 3³ = 27, 3⁴ = 81 → Ans: 243
Type: 14. Date/Day-based Series; Explanation: Progression in dates, months, days of week.; Example: Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun, ? → every 2 days → Ans: Tue
Type: 15. Alphabet Series; Explanation: Series with letters (can be direct or skip pattern).; Example: A, C, E, G, ? → +2 letters → Ans: I
Type: 16. Alphanumeric Series; Explanation: Mix of numbers and letters with pattern.; Example: A1, B2, C3, ? → next: D4
Type: 17. Reverse Series; Explanation: Series progresses in reverse or descending pattern.; Example: 100, 90, 81, 73, ? → -10, -9, -8 → Ans: 66
Type: 18. Square + 1 Series; Explanation: Each term is the square of a number plus 1.; Example: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ? → 1²+1=2, 2²+1=5, 3²+1=10... → Ans: 37
Type: 19. Cube + 1 Series; Explanation: Each term is the cube of a number plus 1.; Example: 2, 9, 28, 65, ? → 1³+1=2, 2³+1=9, 3³+1=28... → Ans: 126
Type; By Sides; By Angles
Equilateral; All sides equal; All angles = 60°
Isosceles; Two sides equal; Two equal angles
Scalene; All sides different; All angles different
Right-Angled - One angle = 90°
Acute - All angles < 90°
Obtuse - One angle > 90°

Formula: Pythagoras Theorem; Expression: a² + b² = c²; Notes: In right-angled triangle; c = hypotenuse
Formula: Heron's Formula; Expression: √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)); Notes: s = (a + b + c)/2 (semi-perimeter)

Concept: Arithmetic Mean (A.M.); Formula: (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) / n; Notes: Simple average
Concept: Geometric Mean (G.M.); Formula: (x₁ × x₂ × ... × xₙ)^(1/n); Notes: nth root of product
Concept: Harmonic Mean (H.M.); Formula: n / [(1/x₁) + (1/x₂) + ... + (1/xₙ)] r; Notes: Reciprocal of average of eciprocals
Concept: Median (Ungrouped); Formula: Middle value (odd n) or avg of two middle (even n); Notes: Data must be in order
Concept: Mode; Formula: Most frequently occurring value; Notes: Can have more than one mode
Type: Sum of first n natural numbers; Formula: S = (n(n + 1)) /2; Example (n = 5): 5(6)/2 = 15
Type: Sum of squares of first n natural numbers; Formula: S = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1)) /6; Example (n = 5): 5(6)(11)/6 = 55
Type: Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers; Formula: S = [n(n + 1)/2]²; Example (n = 5): (15)² = 225
Type: Sum of first n odd numbers; Formula: S = n²; Example (n = 5): 5² = 25
Type: Sum of first n even numbers; Formula: S = n(n + 1); Example (n = 5): 5×6 = 30
Formula: Distance (Speed × Time); Expression: D = S × T; Notes: Basic motion formula
Speed = Distance / Time - S = D / T
Time = Distance / Speed - T = D / S
Average Speed - Total Distance / Total Time

Formula: Average Speed (Equal Distance, Two Speeds); Expression: Avg Speed = (2ab) / (a + b) (where a is speed of going, and b is speed of coming back); Notes: Average Speed (Equal Distance of Going and coming back, with Two different Speeds)
Formula / Rule: Basic Probability; Expression / Formula: P(E) = Favorable Outcomes / Total Outcomes; Explanation: Probability of an event E
Formula / Rule: Impossible Event; Expression / Formula: P = 0; Explanation: Event can never occur
Formula / Rule: Certain Event; Expression / Formula: P = 1; Explanation: Event is guaranteed to occur
Formula / Rule: Complementary Event; Expression / Formula: P(A′) = 1 − P(A); Explanation: Probability of not happening
Formula / Rule: Addition Rule (Mutually Exclusive Events); Expression / Formula: P(A B) = P(A) + P(B); Explanation: A and B cannot occur together
Formula / Rule: Addition Rule (Non-Mutually Exclusive); Expression / Formula: ∪ P(A B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B); Explanation: For overlapping events
Formula / Rule: Multiplication Rule (Independent Events); Expression / Formula: ∪ P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B); Explanation: Occurrence of A doesn't affect B
